look_here_first: Check opposite SIMPLE palmate leaves, then compare sinus depth and leaf undersides: broad 3–5 lobes with relatively shallow notches are typical; short hairs may occur below. Confirm with paired samaras, buds and bark when available. Do not identify from fall color or canyon habitat alone.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Deciduous maple, often in rocky/canyon woodland; growth site supports but cannot prove ID.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Opposite, simple, palmately 3–5-lobed blades; lobes comparatively broad and sinuses often shallower than silver maple; abaxial pubescence varies.

key_traits.label: Flowers
key_traits.text: Small flowers; use twig/bud and paired winged fruits as secondary corroboration.

key_traits.label: Fruits
key_traits.text: Paired winged samaras; young fruits can be hairy. Angle alone is not a decisive species character.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: broader lobes and generally shallower sinuses than silver maple

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: underside can bear short hairs; avoid absolute hair/no-hair rules
